expectations.text: TokenBucket class comment in the .h says what the class is for and states its thread-safety guarantee explicitly
expectations.evidence: Class comment: "Token-bucket rate limiter: tokens accrue continuously at a fixed rate... Thread-safe; all methods may be called concurrently from any thread."

expectations.text: Every public method declaration in the .h has a contract comment: what it does, parameter meaning/units, return value semantics
expectations.evidence: Ctor ("refills at `tokens_per_second` (must be > 0) up to `capacity` tokens... starts full"), Acquire ("Blocks until `n` tokens are available, then consumes them"), TryAcquire ("returns true if... otherwise returns false") all documented; deleted copy ops need no contract.

expectations.text: Acquire documents its blocking semantics (and timeout behavior if a timeout is offered); TryAcquire documents True/False semantics and that nothing is consumed on failure
expectations.evidence: Acquire: "Blocks until `n` tokens are available, then consumes them" (no timeout offered). TryAcquire: "returns true if they are available now; otherwise returns false without consuming anything or blocking."

expectations.text: Units are documented for rates and durations (tokens per second, seconds)
expectations.evidence: Member comment "// Refill rate in tokens per second." and ctor names the parameter `tokens_per_second`; no duration parameters exist in the API.

expectations.text: Function comments are third-person declarative with proper punctuation
expectations.evidence: All start with third-person verbs and end with periods: "Creates a bucket...", "Blocks until...", "Consumes `n` tokens...", "Credits tokens accrued..."

expectations.text: The .cc does not duplicate the .h contract comments; its comments explain implementation choices (e.g. why sleeping outside the lock / condition-variable usage)
expectations.evidence: .cc has no restated contracts; its only comment blocks explain the wait strategy ("No other thread adds tokens; only time does. So rather than waiting for a notification, sleep until the deficit will have accrued...") and the capacity assert.

expectations.text: No comments that restate the code; no Author: lines; // style used consistently
expectations.evidence: No Author: lines anywhere; every comment uses //; member comments add information (units, guarded-by) rather than restating code.

expectations.text: If any call site passes a bare literal argument, it uses the /*param_name=*/value comment form (vacuously true if no such call exists)
expectations.evidence: Vacuously true: no call sites pass bare literals (the `= 1.0` values are default arguments in declarations, not call sites).

expectations.text: Every comment block is at most 3 sentences
expectations.evidence: Counted per block: class comment 2 sentences; ctor 2; Acquire 2; TryAcquire 1; RefillLocked 2; .cc Acquire block 2; all inline comments 1. Maximum is 2.

expectations.text: No usage-example code blocks inside comments
expectations.evidence: No example code appears in any comment in rate_limiter.h or rate_limiter.cc.

summary.notes: Concise, complete Google-style comments: full contracts in the header, implementation rationale only in the .cc, and every block within the CC1 3-sentence limit.
